theater: 長江上游夔州巫山峽口

battle.name: 夔州之戰
battle.theater: 長江上游夔州巫山峽口
battle.brief: 乾德二年冬，宋太祖決策伐後蜀，以曹彬為行營總都督，率禁軍溯長江而上，取江陵為基地，直叩夔州。蜀軍依三峽之險，舟師封江、弩手據岸，宋軍破峽入白帝，順勢趨成都，孟昶出降。卡面羅馬短劍不曾入夔州，它象徵的正是短兵相接的刺擊節奏：登岸後的舟兵與步卒，靠的仍是刀、矛與盾的配合。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是後蜀與北宋兩個政權，戰場在長江上游的川峽一段。北宋方面，決策出自中樞：乾德二年（964）十一月，太祖趙匡胤下詔伐蜀，樞密院掌軍議，曹彬任行營總都督，節制沿江諸軍，劉光世等分道並進；主力是殿前禁軍與荊南、峽路諸州的地方兵，另自江南、淮南、荊湖各州徵發舟船與轉輸之具。後蜀方面，國主孟昶坐成都，樞密院與節度使系統分掌軍政，川東防務倚夔州、歸州、峽州等沿江州縣，蜀中節鎮以劍門一路為北面屏障，夔州則是長江溯流入蜀的門戶。蜀軍沿峽佈防，水軍以舟船封江，岸上築寨置弩，據險而守。曹彬一路走水路，溯長江而上，以江陵為集結與轉輸之地，糧秣裝船隨軍，逆水一段全賴人力挽纖。兩國都承平數十年，兵久不習戰：蜀軍雖據地勢之利，舟弩之制卻久廢，諸說並存；宋軍禁軍新整而熟火器，夾長江糧道而進。
countriesEn: The two belligerents in this war were the Later Shu and the Northern Song, and the fighting took place in a stretch of the upper Yangtze in the Sichuan gorges. On the Song side the decision came from the centre of government: in the eleventh month of the second year of Qiande, 964 AD, the founder Zhao Kuangyin issued the edict to attack Shu, the Privy Council handled the military deliberations, Cao Bin was appointed commander-in-chief of the field camp with authority over all armies on the river, and Liu Guangshi and others advanced by separate routes. The main force was the palace guards together with the local troops of Jingnan and the circuits of the gorge road, and ships and transport were requisitioned from the provinces of Jiangnan, Huainan and Jinghu. On the Later Shu side the ruler Meng Chang sat in Chengdu, the Privy Council and the circuit command system shared the military and civil administration, the eastern defence of the Sichuan rested on the river provinces of Kuizhou, Guizhou and Xiazhou, the circuit garrisons of Shu guarded the northern approach through Jianmen, and Kuizhou itself was the gate through which the Yangtze leads upstream into Sichuan. The Shu army deployed along the gorge, the river force sealing the water with boats while the bank positions were fortified with stockades and crossbows, holding the ground by its natural advantages. Cao Bin took the water route, going up the Yangtze with Jangling as the base for concentration and supply, grain travelling with the army in the boats, and the stretch against the current carried by human haulers on the tow ropes. Both states had been at peace for decades and their troops had long been out of practice: the Shu army held the advantage of position, yet its boats and crossbow service had decayed, and the accounts differ; the Song guards had just been reorganised, were familiar with fire weapons, and advanced along the grain route of the river.
people: 曹彬（931-999），字國華，真定靈壽人，是本役宋軍的總指揮。史稱他治軍嚴謹、行軍不擾，舟師入蜀，所過不妄殺、不掠民，蜀人感之；他也是不走劍門、主張乘舟溯江的主將之一。副手劉光世等分道進兵，兩軍在川峽之間相應；驍騎卒出身的呼延贊，據《宋史》本傳「從王全斌討西川，為前鋒，數創敵」，以衝陣見長，他所造的器械與破陣刀、降魔杵在蜀道狹隘、舟行不進之地最合用，惟其隸屬與出戰編次，各書記載不一。蜀主孟昶在位三十餘年，好聲色、嬉遊、擊球、營造，對宋使者的接待與禮數屢見爭議；孟昶曾遣使議割地，求秦、隴、階、成諸州，宋廷不許，此議遂成兵端。蜀方守夔州、巫山的將領姓名，在《宋史》與《蜀檯稿》之中互見異說，可以確定的只是：夔州至巫山一線由蜀軍重兵把守，蜀師在江上截斷北上的舟路，宋軍自峽中突破。
peopleEn: Cao Bin (931-999), courtesy name Guohua, of Lingshu in Zhending, was the overall commander of the Song army in this campaign. History records that he governed his troops strictly and that his march disturbed no one: when the fleet entered Shu, nothing was killed wantonly and nothing was plundered, and the people of Shu remembered it. He was also one of the commanders who argued for taking the water route by boat up the river instead of the Jianmen road. His subordinates Liu Guangshi and others advanced by separate routes, and the two columns answered one another inside the Sichuan gorges. Huyan Zan, who began as a trooper in the cavalry, is recorded in his biography in the History of Song as having followed Wang Quanbin in the campaign against western Sichuan, serving as the vanguard and winning distinction again and again; the devices he made, together with his armoured-breaking sabre and his iron-headed club, suited the narrow roads of Shu and the places where boats could not advance, though the sources disagree about his unit and the order in which he fought. The Shu ruler Meng Chang had sat on the throne for more than thirty years, given to music, women, ball games and building projects, and the reception and courtesies shown to Song envoys were repeatedly disputed. Meng Chang had sent an envoy to bargain for territory, asking for the provinces of Qin, Long, Jie and Cheng; the Song court refused, and the negotiation became the occasion for war. The names of the Shu commanders holding Kuizhou and Wushan differ between the History of Song and the Shu Platform Draft, and what can be settled is this: the line from Kuizhou to Wushan was held by a strong Shu garrison, the Shu force cut the river route against the boats coming from the north, and the Song army broke through inside the gorge.
kits: 卡面那具羅馬短劍並未出現在夔州；它擺在這張卡上，是要標出短兵相接時「刺」的節奏與盾的配合。蜀與宋的步卒在峽岸、舟橋、登城之際真正能用的，是刀與矛：宋禁軍步卒以步刀、長槊為主，蜀軍步卒用環首刀、戟、槊，兩軍的甲胄以札甲、團牌為要，藤牌、拒馬、鹿角佈於岸線與營門。弩是此役的骨幹：宋軍備有臂力極強的大弩，蜀軍則以弩手倚岸巖列陣，居高射擊江上舟師；宋軍的投石機與弓弩同時向峽中投射，壓制岸上的陣位。火攻見於記載：宋師以火箭焚燒封江的蜀舟，具體經過各書說法不一，但燃燒箭已是此時宋軍常備的火器。舟船既是宋軍的戰具也是糧道：自江陵至夔州水程逾千里，逆流一段需挽夫曳纖，灘險處須人力牽舟；蜀軍以舟船與竹木結構的浮筏扼住峽口，在舟上列弩拒敵。攻城用飛梯、搭棚與穴進之具，轉輸用征自江南、荊湖的民船與漕舟，隨軍還帶足夠七日之糧。
kitsEn: The Roman short sword on the card never appeared at Kuizhou; it is placed there to mark the rhythm of the thrust and the work of the shield in close fighting. What the infantry of Shu and Song could really use on the bank, on the gangway and at the walls was the knife and the spear: the Song guard infantry were armed with sabres and long spears, the Shu infantry with ring-pommel swords, halberds and spears, and both sides relied on lamellar armour and round shields, with rattan shields, cheval-de-frise and abatis laid along the bank line and in front of the camp gates. The crossbow was the backbone of the engagement: the Song brought crossbows of very heavy draw, while the Shu posted crossbowmen along the cliff banks to shoot down on the boats below, and the Song trebuchets and bows worked together on the gorge, pressing the enemy positions on the bank. Fire attack appears in the records: the Song used fire arrows to burn the Shu boats that sealed the river, though the accounts differ over the exact course of it; by then the fire arrow was already a standard weapon in the Song camp. The boats were both weapon and supply line for the Song army: the water distance from Jangling to Kuizhou runs well over a thousand li, and the stretch against the current required haulers on the tow ropes, with men pulling the boats through the shallows; the Shu held the mouth of the gorge with boats and with rafts built of bamboo and timber, and put crossbowmen on the boats to bar the way. For the assault they had scaling ladders, mantlets to bridge the wall and picks to work under it, and for supply they carried the privately owned boats and the grain junks requisitioned in Jiangnan and Jinghu, together with enough grain for seven days on the march.
tactics: 宋軍的進攻次序是「先水後陸、破峽而入」。第一步是取江陵：乾德元年（963）平荊南之後，長江中游在宋手，川峽的東戶洞開。第二步是集舟：各州徵發的船與禁軍在江陵會合，軍資糧秣裝船，溯江而上，途中不與蜀軍主力接戰，專取舟行的速度。第三步是攻峽：至夔州、巫山一線，蜀軍以舟封江、岸上築壘，弩手居高臨下；宋軍以弩砲與投石機壓制岸上陣位，使火火箭得其際會，焚其舟船，然後以輕舟與敢死之士自上流夜間而下，或強渡登岸，逼其退保白帝城。登岸之後，短兵相接的時刻到來：舟兵與步卒在灘頭、碼頭、營門互相砍刺，卡面短劍所象徵的正是這種以刺代劈、以盾護身的打法；峽道逼仄，兵力展不開，一支先鋒插入即可決定一段江面的歸屬。第四步是乘破竹之勢直趨成都，孟昶出降。蜀軍的對應全在「守險」二字：以舟封江、以壘節節抵抗、倚峽岸弩石齊下，把縱深換成時間；然而峽道同時限制守方的退路，最終被宋軍沿江逐段吃掉。
tacticsEn: The order of the Song attack was water first, land second, and the breach made inside the gorge. The first step was the taking of Jangling: after Jingnan was pacified in the first year of Qiande, 963 AD, the middle Yangtze was in Song hands and the eastern door of the Sichuan gorge stood open. The second step was the concentration of boats: the ships requisitioned from the provinces and the palace guards were assembled at Jangling, the military stores and grain were loaded, and the army went up the river without engaging the main Shu force, taking its speed from the water. The third step was the assault in the gorge. At the line from Kuizhou to Wushan the Shu sealed the river with boats and raised stockades on the bank, with crossbowmen looking down from above. The Song answered with bolt-throwers and trebuchets, pressing the bank positions so that the fire arrows found their moment and burned the boats; then light craft and volunteers forlorn came down from the upper reaches by night, or forced a landing, driving the defenders back to Baidi. Once ashore, the moment of close fighting arrived: boat troops and infantry struck at the landing places, the wharves and the camp gates. What the short sword on the card stands for is exactly this way of fighting, the thrust in place of the slash and the shield guarding the body. The gorge road is narrow, ranks cannot be deployed, and a single vanguard thrust can decide the ownership of a stretch of water. The fourth step was to ride the momentum straight to Chengdu, where Meng Chang surrendered. The Shu answer lay entirely in holding the danger: boats sealing the river, stockades resisting in succession, bolts and stones from the cliff banks, trading depth for time. Yet the same gorge road also fenced in the defenders, and they were eaten up stretch by stretch as the Song army worked its way up the river.
data: 可核對的日期與數字散見《宋史·曹彬傳》《續資治通鑑》與《宋會要》。乾德二年即964年：十一月宋太祖下詔伐蜀，舟師自江陵溯流而上；十二月宋軍破夔州、巫山之險，進逼白帝城；乾德三年正月孟昶遣使奉表請降，其後宋軍入成都，後蜀亡。自出兵到入蜀，前後約三個月，而江陵至成都的水程逾千里，逆水行舟、挽纖灘險，是這條戰線最大的時耗。兵力的規模，各書稱宋發禁軍及沿江諸州兵以數萬計，徵自江南、荊湖、淮南的舟船數千艘，蜀軍沿江屯兵亦以數萬計，但具體名額與分道兵力的數字，今存史料並無統一記載，姑存其概。糧秣方面，蜀地是五代諸國中最厚之邦，成都與沿江州縣尚有倉儲可以支應，宋軍則靠江南、荊湖的船運接濟；蜀亡之後，宋室所得的府庫、圖籍、兵器與熟習上游水路的蜀兵，成為十年後平南唐的資本。器械方面，火箭、弩砲、投石機與槊、刀、盾各按其常規規格配發，至於射程、射界與每日發射的數目，史無明文，不宜臆造。
dataEn: The dates and figures that can be checked are scattered through the biography of Cao Bin in the History of Song, the Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror and the Collected Essentials of Song. The second year of Qiande was 964 AD: in the eleventh month the founder Zhao Kuangyin issued the edict against Shu and the fleet went up the river from Jangling; in the twelfth month the Song army broke the danger of Kuizhou and Wushan and pressed on to Baidi; in the first month of the third year of Qiande Meng Chang sent an envoy with a petition for surrender, and afterwards the Song army entered Chengdu, and the Later Shu was ended. From the order to march to the entry into Shu the whole thing took about three months, while the water distance from Jangling to Chengdu runs well over a thousand li, and going up the river with the boats, towing them through the shallows, was the largest drain of time on this front. As for the size of the armies, the books speak of some tens of thousands of Song guards and provincial troops along the river, of several thousand ships requisitioned in Jiangnan, Jinghu and Huainan, and of a Shu force on the river likewise counted in tens of thousands; but the exact figures and the strength of each column have no uniform record in the surviving histories, so only the rough outline can stand. As to supply, Shu was the wealthiest of the states of the Five Dynasties, the granaries of Chengdu and of the river provinces could still feed a campaign, and the Song drew on the shipping of Jiangnan and Jinghu; after the fall of Shu, the treasuries, the registers, the weapons and the boat-handling troops of Shu became the capital that paid for the conquest of Southern Tang ten years later. As for the arms, fire arrows, bolt-throwers, trebuchets, spears, sabres and shields were issued to their normal specifications, but their ranges, their fields of fire and their daily rate of fire are simply not on record, and no figures should be invented for them.
cause: 開戰的起因有三層。第一層是北方的統一計劃：宋已於乾德元年平荊南，長江中游在手，下一步若要取南唐、掃平江南，就必須先定蜀之西翼，免得兩面受敵；蜀據劍門之險，本難攻取，宋廷因此需要蜀地內外交困的時機。第二層是蜀的失禮與外交僵局：孟昶好聲色而輕邊事，遣使議割地，求秦、隴、階、成諸州，宋廷不許；使者往返，禮數與稱辭屢有爭議，兩國名分之爭由是轉為兵端。第三層是雙方內部的鬆動：蜀地雖厚，軍備久弛，沿江舟弩之制屢經裁汰，州縣守將各懷自保之心；宋則禁軍新整，連平荊南、南漢諸處，兵心可用。於是乾德二年冬，太祖以為蜀兵未練而宋軍精熟，遂發兵。分道安排也說明宋廷並非只押一條路：以曹彬走峽路，取水軍之便與糧道之捷，另一路則取陸路，出益州之後，兩道在川峽之間互相策應。
causeEn: The war began for three reasons, one above the other. The first was the northern programme of unification: the Song had already pacified Jingnan in the first year of Qiande, the middle Yangtze was in its hands, and if it was to take Southern Tang and level the south it had first to settle the western flank of Shu, so as not to be pressed from two sides. Shu was protected by the difficulty of Jianmen and hard to attack, so the Song court needed a moment when Shu was pinched from within and without. The second was the discourtesy of Shu and the deadlock in diplomacy. Meng Chang gave himself to pleasure and took border matters lightly, sent an envoy to bargain for territory, asking for Qin, Long, Jie and Cheng, and the Song court refused. As envoys went back and forth, the courtesies and the forms of address were disputed again and again, and the argument over who held the proper title turned into the occasion for war. The third was the loosening inside both states. Shu was rich, but its armament had long been neglected, the boat and crossbow service on the river had been cut back repeatedly, and the commanders of the provinces were each thinking of their own safety; the Song guards had just been reorganised, had just taken Jingnan and Southern Han, and their fighting spirit was usable. So in the winter of the second year of Qiande the founder, judging that the Shu troops were untrained and the Song soldiers practised, gave the order to march. The division of the army into columns shows that the court did not stake everything on one road: Cao Bin took the gorge road for the convenience of the fleet and the speed of the grain route, while another column moved by land behind Yizhou, and the two answered one another inside the Sichuan gorges.
impact: 夔州一破，蜀的門戶洞開，後蜀的覆亡已成定局，直接的結果是蜀地歸宋，五代以來割據半壁的格局被打破。從財政與軍力看，此役使宋室得到五代最厚的財賦與糧秣，也得到一批熟習上游水戰的蜀兵與舟船；開寶七年（975）滅南唐，江南財賴以北運，遂成定局，川蜀所出的銅、鹽、絲、錦，成為北宋前期的重要稅源與軍資。從制度看，蜀地舊有的節鎮體制在平蜀之後被大幅削弱，朝廷得以直接派文臣與禁軍鎮之，「先南後北」的統一次序由此確立。從兵器看，此役是唐宋之際兵器換代的一次現場：弩砲與投石機第一次同時壓制對岸，火火箭由隨軍雜器變成水戰的常備手段，盾牌的用法也從遮蔽城牆轉向結舟隊與護登岸線。有一點必須說明：卡面那具羅馬短劍是本案的象徵物，不是此戰的實物，它提醒人們的是——真正決定峽江歸屬的，仍是舟船、弩砲與背水一戰的士氣。
impactEn: Once Kuizhou fell the door of Shu stood open and the end of the Later Shu was settled; the immediate result was that Shu came under the Song and the pattern of a half-empire of separate regimes that had held since the Five Dynasties was broken. In fiscal and military terms the campaign gave the Song house the richest resources and grain of the Five Dynasties, and also a body of Shu troops and boats that knew the upper river; with the fall of Southern Tang in the seventh year of Kaibao, 975, the wealth of the south began to move north, and the copper, salt, silk and brocade of the Sichuan region became an important source of tax and military supply for the early Northern Song. In institutional terms the old circuit system of Shu was sharply reduced after the conquest, the court was able to post civil officials and palace guards directly, and the order of unification, south first and north afterwards, was thereby established. In the history of arms the campaign is a moment of transition between the weapon systems of the Tang and the Song: bolt-throwers and trebuchets pressed the far bank for the first time together, the fire arrow changed from a miscellaneous piece of camp baggage into a standard weapon of river warfare, and the shield changed from covering a city wall to being used to close up boat formations and to cover the line of a landing. One point must be made plainly: the Roman short sword on the card is an emblem for this case and not an object that fought in it, and what it reminds us of is that what really decided the ownership of the gorge was the boats, the bolt-throwers and the morale of men fighting with their backs to the river.
result: 結果分三段。第一段是夔州與峽路：宋軍破蜀舟於峽中，取夔州、巫山、白帝城，蜀軍節節退保，成都的北面屏障與東面門戶同時失守。第二段是成都：乾德三年正月，孟昶奉表請降，宋軍入成都，後蜀亡；自孟知祥建蜀至此，後蜀歷二主、三十餘年而終。孟昶出降後封王，遷居京師，未幾而卒，蜀宮府庫、圖籍、兵械悉為宋有，蜀兵多編入禁軍與諸州鎮兵。第三段是善後與秩序：宋廷以禁軍鎮蜀，削節度之權，置官改易州縣之名，並把上游水道的航運與漕運納入新朝版籍。就戰役本身而言，蜀軍在峽中的抵抗並非無效——封江、列弩、築壘都曾使宋軍舟師受阻——但沒有扭轉攻守的大勢；反而是宋軍把舟師、弩砲、火器與敢死突擊結成一套，越過了三峽這道從來未被北方王朝正面突破過的關口。夔州之戰因此成為北宋統一南方諸國中最短、最少折損的關鍵一役。
resultEn: The outcome came in three stages. The first was Kuizhou and the gorge road: the Song fleet burned the Shu boats in the gorge, took Kuizhou, Wushan and Baidi, and the Shu army fell back stage by stage, so that the northern screen of Chengdu and its eastern gate were lost at the same time. The second was Chengdu: in the first month of the third year of Qiande Meng Chang sent in a petition for surrender, the Song army entered the city, and the Later Shu was ended; counting from the founding of Shu by Meng Zhixiang, the house had lasted two rulers and a little over thirty years. After his surrender Meng Chang was made a prince and moved to the capital, where he died within the year; the treasuries, the registers and the arms of the Shu palace passed to the Song, and many Shu soldiers were incorporated into the guards and the provincial garrisons. The third was the settlement and the new order: the Song garrisoned Shu with the palace guards, cut the authority of the circuit commanders, changed the names of the offices and the counties, and brought the navigation and transport of the upper river into the registers of the new dynasty. As for the battle itself, the Shu defence inside the gorge was not without effect: sealing the river, lining the banks with crossbows and raising stockades all held up the Song boats for a time, but none of it turned the balance of attack and defence. It was the Song army that tied boats, bolt-throwers, fire weapons and the volunteer assault into a single system and carried it through the Three Gorges, a barrier that no northern dynasty had ever before broken by direct assault. In that sense the battle of Kuizhou was the shortest and least costly of the key engagements by which the Northern Song unified the southern states.
